text:
Bitcoin remained trapped in a tight $65,051–$65,800 channel as the $2.28 trillion crypto market recorded a Fear & Greed reading of 22 (Extreme Fear). The cautious trading environment stems directly from the conclusion of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting under new Chair Kevin Warsh. Markets priced a near-certain hold of the federal funds rate at 3.50%–3.75%, driven by headline inflation accelerating to 4.2%. Concurrently, institutional infrastructure continues to expand globally, marked by Kraken's launch of CFTC-regulated perpetual futures and Hong Kong's passage of a 2027 crypto tax reporting framework.

The Federal Reserve's anticipated removal of its easing bias has solidified a higher-for-longer regime, presenting a stark headwind for non-yielding digital assets. As U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs record sustained outflows, institutional capital is aggressively rotating into AI equities, pushing the Dow above 52,000. Ultimately, until the Fed signals a pivot from inflation-fighting measures, Bitcoin's upside remains heavily constrained by the magnetic pull of risk-free rates and a resilient U.S. dollar.
